structure.heading: FY2025 Consolidated Financial Performance and Shareholder Returns
text_content: **FY2025 Consolidated Financial Performance and Shareholder Returns**

FY2025 consolidated revenue was $24.6B, an increase of 12% year-over-year, reflecting broad-based demand across the Company's end markets. Growth was driven by higher volume and favorable pricing in key product lines, with particularly strong performance in North America and Asia-Pacific. The revenue expansion delivered meaningful operating leverage and supported incremental investment in research and go-to-market capabilities. The Executive Leadership Team attributes the topline improvement to disciplined commercial execution, channel expansion, and greater cross-sell penetration among enterprise customers during the fiscal year and stable supply chain execution throughout FY2025.

Operating performance improved materially in FY2025, with operating margin expanding to 21.4%, an increase of 180 basis points year-over-year, driven by cost discipline and productivity initiatives. The margin expansion reflects a combination of fixed-cost absorption from higher revenue, targeted SG&A savings, and manufacturing efficiency gains implemented across the global footprint. Pricing actions and mix shift toward higher-margin offerings contributed incrementally. The Finance organization implemented enhanced cost controls and monthly performance metrics, enabling the Company to translate revenue growth into sustained margin improvement without compromising strategic investments during FY2025.

Diluted earnings per share for FY2025 were $4.18, up 19% year-over-year, reflecting higher operating income and disciplined capital allocation. EPS growth was supported by net income expansion and the effect of share count reductions realized over the period, enhancing return per outstanding share. The Board of Directors remains focused on delivering long-term shareholder value through a balanced approach that prioritizes reinvestment for growth, prudent M&A where accretive, and returning cash to shareholders. The Company will continue to review capital deployment to maintain flexibility and pursue shareholder-friendly outcomes strategically.

structure.heading: Segment Performance Drivers and FY2026 Investor Guidance Framework
text_content: **Segment Performance Drivers and FY2026 Investor Guidance Framework**

Cloud & Data Platform performance in FY2025 was driven by higher ARR and expanded consumption: revenue reached $10.2B with a 28.6% segment operating margin. Key drivers included enterprise migrations to hybrid deployments, increased AI workload utilization, pricing tiers that capture value from outcomes, and operational efficienices from consolidation of data services. Continued margin discipline supported reinvestment in R&D.

International operations contributed $9.1B in FY2025, representing 37% of total revenue, reflecting growth across EMEA and APAC. Performance drivers encompassed localized go-to-market motions, channel expansion, and pricing optimization amid FX movement. Investment in customer success, compliance capabilities, and partnerships accelerated go-to-customer velocity and improved contract renewals and net retention.

For FY2026 we have issued guidance of $26.9B–$27.5B in revenue and diluted EPS of $4.55–$4.75. The investor guidance framework ties these targets to milestones: 1) subscription ARR growth, 2) margin preservation through productivity programs, and 3) disciplined capital allocation. Sensitivity aanlyses published with updates will quantify the impact of macro and currency scenarios. Management will host a webcast Feb. 15, 2026.

spec.title: Aurora Systems, Inc. — Annual Report
spec.subtitle: Form 10-K Summary | Fiscal Year Ended December 31, 2025

sections.heading: FY2025 Financial Highlights
sections.body: Aurora Systems delivered full-year revenue of $8.74 billion, an increase of 14.2% compared to FY2024, driven by sustained enterprise demand and expanding subscription renewals. Operating income rose to $1.96 billion, resulting in an operating margin of 22.4%, up 240 basis points year over year. Diluted earnings per share reached $4.87, reflecting both margin expansion and disciplined share repurchases totaling $320 million during the fiscal year.

sections.heading: Segment Performance
sections.body: The Cloud & Data Platform segment led performance with revenue growth of 26% to $3.58 billion, supported by new AI-enabled analytics deployments and higher consumption across existing accounts. Segment operating margin expanded to 31.6%, underscoring strong incremental profitability. The Enterprise Applications segment grew 6% to $3.12 billion, while Network & Edge Solutions remained stable at $2.04 billion amid softer telecom infrastructure spending.

sections.heading: Cash Flow and Capital Allocation
sections.body: Operating cash flow for FY2025 was $2.21 billion, representing 25% of revenue, with free cash flow conversion of 92% of net income. The company reduced net debt by $410 million and ended the year with $1.3 billion in cash and equivalents. Management increased the quarterly dividend by 8% and authorized an additional $500 million for share repurchases.

sections.heading: FY2026 Outlook
sections.body: For FY2026, management expects revenue between $9.35 billion and $9.55 billion, implying growth of 7% to 9% despite a moderating macroeconomic environment. Operating margin is projected to expand modestly to approximately 23%, supported by continued Cloud & Data Platform mix shift. Diluted EPS is anticipated in the range of $5.20 to $5.35, assuming stable foreign exchange rates and ongoing cost discipline.

Macro note: enterprise deal cycles elongating slightly in EMEA.
Capex planned ~$950M for data center expansion + AI compute capacity.
Key message: durable, margin-accretive growth model validated.

sections.heading: Executive Overview
sections.body: Fiscal 2025 marked a year of broad-based, margin-accretive growth across all operating segments, led by exceptional performance in Cloud & Data Platform. Consolidated revenue increased 14.8% year over year to $9.74 billion, supported by durable enterprise demand and improved pricing discipline. Operating income rose 22.3% to $1.86 billion, reflecting scale efficiencies and disciplined cost management. Diluted earnings per share expanded 27% to $3.42, underscoring the earnings leverage embedded in our portfolio.

sections.heading: Segment Performance
sections.body: Cloud & Data Platform revenue advanced 26% to $4.12 billion, with segment operating margin improving 340 basis points to 31.5%, driven by higher subscription mix and optimized infrastructure spend. The Digital Applications segment delivered 9% growth to $3.05 billion, while maintaining a healthy 24% margin despite ongoing R&D investments. Legacy Systems declined 3% to $1.27 billion but generated stable cash flows and a 19% operating margin. International markets represented 38% of total revenue, up from 35% in the prior year.

sections.heading: Profitability and Cash Flow
sections.body: Gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 62.8%, reflecting favorable mix shift toward recurring cloud services and automation-driven cost efficiencies. Adjusted EBITDA reached $2.34 billion, up 19% year over year. Operating cash flow totaled $2.01 billion, enabling $620 million in share repurchases and $410 million in strategic tuck-in acquisitions. Net leverage declined to 1.4x EBITDA at year-end, strengthening balance sheet flexibility.

sections.heading: Capital Allocation and Shareholder Returns
sections.body: The Board approved a 12% increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.28 per share, marking the sixth consecutive year of dividend growth. During FY2025, the company repurchased 8.3 million shares under its existing authorization, contributing approximately $0.11 to EPS accretion. Capital expenditures of $540 million were primarily directed toward data center expansion and AI-enabled product capabilities. Management remains committed to a balanced capital allocation framework prioritizing growth investments and disciplined shareholder returns.

sections.heading: FY2026 Outlook
sections.body: For fiscal 2026, management projects revenue in the range of $10.6–$10.9 billion, representing growth of 9–12%, assuming a moderating macroeconomic environment. Operating margin is expected to expand modestly to approximately 20%, supported by continued cloud mix shift and productivity initiatives. Diluted EPS is anticipated between $3.75 and $3.95, reflecting sustained margin expansion and capital return impact. While demand patterns remain uneven in certain enterprise verticals, pipeline visibility and renewal rates provide confidence in durable, profitable growth.

structure.full_text:
Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Highlights and Outlook
FY Ended 31 December 2025 | Investor Update | Issued 18 February 2026

Section Executive Overview
Fiscal 2025 marked a year of broad-based, margin-accretive growth across all operating segments, led by exceptional performance in Cloud & Data Platform. Consolidated revenue increased 14.8% year over year to $9.74 billion, supported by durable enterprise demand and improved pricing discipline. Operating income rose 22.3% to $1.86 billion, reflecting scale efficiencies and disciplined cost management. Diluted earnings per share expanded 27% to $3.42, underscoring the earnings leverage embedded in our portfolio.

Section Segment Performance
Cloud & Data Platform revenue advanced 26% to $4.12 billion, with segment operating margin improving 340 basis points to 31.5%, driven by higher subscription mix and optimized infrastructure spend. The Digital Applications segment delivered 9% growth to $3.05 billion, while maintaining a healthy 24% margin despite ongoing R&D investments. Legacy Systems declined 3% to $1.27 billion but generated stable cash flows and a 19% operating margin. International markets represented 38% of total revenue, up from 35% in the prior year.

Section Profitability and Cash Flow
Gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 62.8%, reflecting favorable mix shift toward recurring cloud services and automation-driven cost efficiencies. Adjusted EBITDA reached $2.34 billion, up 19% year over year. Operating cash flow totaled $2.01 billion, enabling $620 million in share repurchases and $410 million in strategic tuck-in acquisitions. Net leverage declined to 1.4x EBITDA at year-end, strengthening balance sheet flexibility.

Section Capital Allocation and Shareholder Returns
The Board approved a 12% increase in the quarterly dividend to $0.28 per share, marking the sixth consecutive year of dividend growth. During FY2025, the company repurchased 8.3 million shares under its existing authorization, contributing approximately $0.11 to EPS accretion. Capital expenditures of $540 million were primarily directed toward data center expansion and AI-enabled product capabilities. Management remains committed to a balanced capital allocation framework prioritizing growth investments and disciplined shareholder returns.

Section FY2026 Outlook
For fiscal 2026, management projects revenue in the range of $10.6–$10.9 billion, representing growth of 9–12%, assuming a moderating macroeconomic environment. Operating margin is expected to expand modestly to approximately 20%, supported by continued cloud mix shift and productivity initiatives. Diluted EPS is anticipated between $3.75 and $3.95, reflecting sustained margin expansion and capital return impact. While demand patterns remain uneven in certain enterprise verticals, pipeline visibility and renewal rates provide confidence in durable, profitable growth.

Confidential — For Institutional Investors and Analysts | Page 1 of 1
